10_000_tickets.query_latency: Query time is dominated by **ONNX query embedding** (CPU) and Python client overhead, not HNSW search. At 200 tickets, retrieval is sub-second and was not the hybrid latency bottleneck (Section 11).
10_000_tickets.recall_implications: HNSW with search_ef=10 is typically near-exact at this size; retrieval quality issues (e.g. order 10864 RR 0.0–0.5) are embedding/semantic, not index-approximation error.
10_000_tickets.operational_ops: Full rebuild (`delete_collection` + `add`) is acceptable at this size.

1_000_000_tickets.query_latency: HNSW search cost grows ~O(log n); expect milliseconds to tens of ms for ANN search on one collection. Query embedding still runs per request. Tune `hnsw:search_ef` upward if recall drops.
1_000_000_tickets.recall_implications: **Approximate** — default search_ef=10 trades recall for speed. Theme queries with dozens of relevant tickets (Section 6) become harder to fully recall at small K regardless.
1_000_000_tickets.operational_ops: Full rebuild gets slow (re-embed all tickets). Need `upsert` batches or partitioned collections (by date/customer) for incremental ingest.

10_000_000_tickets.query_latency: Single monolithic HNSW index may need sharding, dedicated embedding service, and higher search_ef. Consider metadata pre-filtering (customer_id, order_id) before vector search to shrink candidate set.
10_000_000_tickets.recall_implications: ANN recall vs latency tradeoff becomes operational. Exact brute-force is not viable. Hybrid graph path becomes more important for identifier-heavy queries (order numbers).
10_000_000_tickets.operational_ops: Require streaming upsert pipeline, tombstone deletes, and consistency contract with Neo4j ticket nodes.
